description: We are a team of ambitious innovators from Kyrgyzstan passionate about space, science, and technology. Combining creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving, we aim to turn ideas into practical solutions using NASA data and emerging technologies. We believe innovation has no borders and are excited to contribute our perspective to the global NASA Space Apps Challenge community.
summary:
Overview & How It Works
Fire Calendar: Kyrgyzstan is an interactive web application that monitors and visualizes wildfire and thermal anomaly patterns across Kyrgyzstan. Using NASA MODIS and VIIRS satellite data, it displays daily fire detections through a calendar heatmap, historical charts (2010–2025), and an interactive map. Users can filter data by sensor, year, day/night, and geographic coordinates, as well as export results in CSV format.
 Benefits & Intended Impact
Wildfires and agricultural burning threaten Kyrgyzstan’s ecosystems, air quality, and communities. Our platform makes satellite data easier to understand, helping researchers, ecologists, authorities, and citizens identify seasonal fire peaks, compare current activity with historical trends, and recognize high-risk areas without specialized GIS software.

 Tools & Technologies
- **Data:** NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS).
- **Frontend:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript.
- **Mapping:** Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.
- **Deployment:** Netlify.

 Creativity & Key Factors
Our main innovation is combining a calendar heatmap, interactive map, and historical comparisons in one platform. We also address sensor bias: VIIRS was introduced alongside MODIS in 2012, increasing total detection counts. Users can filter sensors separately to make more accurate year-to-year comparisons.
details:
Overview & How It Works

Fire Calendar: Kyrgyzstan is an interactive web application designed to monitor, analyze, and visualize wildfire and thermal anomaly patterns across Kyrgyzstan. Using open-source Earth observation datasets from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellites, the platform displays daily fire detections in an intuitive calendar heatmap format alongside multi-year statistical charts (2010–2025) and an interactive map. Users can filter detections by sensor, year, day/night cycles, and custom geographic coordinates, as well as export raw hotspot points and analytics in CSV format. 

Benefits & Intended Impact

Wildfires and agricultural burning pose significant threats to Kyrgyzstan’s mountainous ecosystems, air quality, and local communities. Our tool transforms complex satellite telemetry into accessible, actionable insights. It empowers ecologists, researchers, local authorities, and citizens to easily spot seasonal peaks, compare current fire activity against historical medians, and identify high-risk regions without needing specialized GIS software. 

Tools & Technologies Used

Data Sources: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) — MODIS and VIIRS active fire data. 

Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Leaflet / OpenStreetMap for interactive geospatial mapping. 

Deployment: Hosted via Netlify for fast, global accessibility. 

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Instead of presenting satellite data solely as a cluttered map, we combined a calendar heatmap with historical baseline comparisons (such as median anomaly percentages). A critical factor our team accounted for is sensor bias: because VIIRS data was added alongside MODIS starting in 2012, raw detection counts naturally increased. Our interface explicitly highlights this nuance and allows users to toggle individual sensors to ensure fair, scientifically accurate year-over-year comparisons
